claim: Moving the same Qwen2.5-3B / 4-rank job from NVLink A100 to PCIe L4 raises ZeRO-2's NCCL share of kernel time from 17.3% to 50.2% and FSDP2 reshard's from 27.7% to 51.1%, i.e. communication becomes roughly half of kernel time once the wire is PCIe.
stance_target: The premise that sharded data-parallel collectives become a first-order cost on a thin wire
scope_conditions: Qwen2.5-3B bf16, micro-batch 1, seq 2048, 4 ranks, 15 steps median, n=1, defaults-vs-defaults; 4x A100 40GB NVLink vs 4x L4 24GB PCIe
quoted_support: On PCIe, the NCCL share rises sharply for most configs (FSDP2 no-reshard 26.1%->46.7%, ZeRO-2 17.3%->50.2%)

claim: On the PCIe L4 run ZeRO-2 still reaches 1,923 tok/s and beats FSDP2 no-reshard's 1,761 tok/s, so a 50% NCCL kernel-time share does not translate into a >50% throughput penalty.
stance_target: Equating a 50% NCCL kernel-duration share with a 50% step-time overhead
scope_conditions: Same matrix; author caveat that NCCL share 'does not map one-to-one onto pure communication-wait time'
quoted_support: Note: the NCCL share is the ratio of NCCL kernel duration reported by the profiler; communication overlaps with compute, so it does not map one-to-one onto pure communication-wait time in wall-clock terms.

claim: The matrix contains no DDP baseline at all: ZeRO-0 (pure replication) OOMs even on a 40 GB A100 with 30.01 GB resident before activations, so this study cannot produce a ZeRO-2-vs-DDP step-time ratio.
stance_target: Whether this source can settle cc-3(a)
quoted_support: ZeRO-0 (no sharding) | OOM ... this process has 30.01 GiB memory in use.

claim: On PCIe the sharding ranking flips: ZeRO-3 (2,290 tok/s) comes out ~19% ahead of ZeRO-2 (1,923 tok/s), the reverse of the A100 ranking where ZeRO-2 leads ZeRO-3 by 2.1x.
stance_target: The assumption that the NVLink-tuned ZeRO-2 recommendation transfers unchanged to a thin wire
scope_conditions: Same matrix; author states the cause (memory pressure vs collective scheduling) is not settled
quoted_support: On L4, ZeRO-3 (2,290 tok/s) comes out ~19% ahead of ZeRO-2 (1,923 tok/s) — the reverse of the A100 ranking.
